observation_summary: The compiler failed to process @lends annotations when the object literal was defined in the same statement as the class, because the type-checking logic expected the class to be declared beforehand.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the procedural logic of how object literals are processed. Instead of immediately calling 'defineObjectLiteral(n)', the code now buffers object literals with @lends annotations in a list ('lentObjectLiterals') and processes them later once the statement is fully analyzed. This is a change to the algorithmic strategy for handling type definitions, not a simple guard or initialization fix.
evidence_used: The fix introduces a new list 'lentObjectLiterals' to buffer object literals.
The fix modifies the 'attachLiteralTypes' method to defer processing of @lends object literals.
The fix adds a new block in the statement analysis to process the buffered 'lentObjectLiterals' after the statement is parsed.
The bug report states that @lends does not work unless the class is defined beforehand, indicating a procedural limitation in the compiler's analysis order.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While this adds a new capability (supporting inline @lends), the fix is implemented as a local procedural change to the existing type-checking algorithm rather than a design-level architectural change.

The fix ensures that the object literal definition is correctly associated with the class declaration, but the root cause is the order of operations in the algorithm, not a broken structural association.
